title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞} is modelled linearly through the classical identification of the free group on l_0, l_1 with Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z). Here l_0 = [[1,−2],[0,1]] and l_1 is lower-unipotent. This gives a congruence ('adelic') shadow inside SL(2,Ẑ) and GL(2,Ẑ)' = GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. The group M^{!~}_{0,3} is a Teichmüller/GT-type group of automorphisms. Its elements are encoded, Drinfeld/Ihara style, by a pair (ξ,η) of 'cocycle' elements: ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, with ρ the order-3 symmetry and σ_∞ an order-2 symmetry. The previous page showed three things: ξ and u_ξ determine each other (163 bis); u ↦ [u,ρ] = uρ(u)^{-1} is a 1-cocycle on the Borel-type group B = {[[μ,M],[0,1]] : μ ∈ Ẑ^*, M ∈ Ẑ}; and M^{!~}_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' is a homomorphism.

This page.
(173)–(174): from now on Grothendieck parametrizes the pair (ξ,η), seen from the adelic viewpoint, by the single matrix u = [[μ,M],[0,1]] ∈ B. One has M ≡ 0 mod 2 when u comes from the subgroup M^{!~}_{0,3}(0). One recovers ξ = [u,ρ] and η = [u,σ_∞].

He then remarks: as long as one does not use the unique non-linear factorizations ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} (α ∈ Π̂~, β ∈ Π̂), the only adelic invariants naturally attached to an element are (ξ,η), or equivalently and 'more prettily' u.

(175)–(176): the inner elements λ = l_0^n ∈ L_0 give ξ = η = l_0^n l_1^{-n} = [[1+4n²,−2n],[−2n,1]], and their matrix is λ = l_0^n = [[1,−2n],[0,1]].

(177): left multiplication gives l_0^n · [[μ,M],[0,1]] = [[μ,M−2n],[0,1]]. So L_0 acts by translating M by even amounts.

The sentence is completed on the next page. Let B_1 = {M ≡ 0 mod 2}. Then B_1/L_0 ≅ T_0 = {diag(μ,1)}, and B_1 is the semidirect product L_0 ⋊ T_0. This yields a canonical splitting of the extension M^{!~}(0) → N^{!~} = M^{!~}(0)/L_0. The only arithmetic invariant surviving on the quotient is the multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ^*, i.e. the cyclotomic-character-like component.

Purpose: to understand how much of a GT/Galois-type element is detected by its 'linear' (congruence-quotient) image, and to normalize representatives modulo inner automorphisms by l_0.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Checked: (175) gives det = 1, and the product [[1,−2n],[0,1]][[1,0],[−2n,1]] = [[1+4n²,−2n],[−2n,1]] is correct; (177) is correct.

The sign conventions are slightly asymmetric: l_0 = [[1,−2],[0,1]] while l_1^{-n} = [[1,0],[−2n,1]], i.e. l_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]]. This is presumably chosen to fit a relation of the form l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1 and is not an error.
The identity ξ = η for λ = l_0^n tacitly uses that both ρ and σ_∞ send l_0 to l_1 (at least in the linear image). This is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Encoding the pair of cocycle data (ξ,η) of a GT-type automorphism by a single upper-triangular matrix u = [[μ,M],[0,1]] in GL(2,Ẑ), via ξ = [u,ρ] and η = [u,σ_∞].
ideas.modern_name: Image of (λ,f)-type GT data in the congruence quotient PSL(2,Ẑ) of the Γ(2) model of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for (λ,f) parametrizations; the congruence-quotient picture is folklore in the GT literature.

ideas.what: Inner automorphisms by powers of l_0 act on u by M ↦ M − 2n. Hence B_1/L_0 ≅ T_0, giving the semidirect decomposition B_1 = L_0 ⋊ T_0 and a canonical normal form u = diag(μ,1).
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of GT elements modulo inner automorphisms; Borel = unipotent ⋊ torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Borel decomposition); the normalization of GT elements modulo inner automorphisms is standard in Drinfeld/Ihara.

ideas.what: Observation that the only adelic invariant visible in the linear model, modulo L_0, is the multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ^*.
ideas.modern_name: The action on the congruence/modular tower factors through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Shimura, and Kronecker–Weber for the modular tower; Ihara and others in the GT context.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, correct bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's linear (congruence) model of GT-type groups: a parametrization by Borel matrices and a normal form modulo inner automorphisms. The conclusion, that only the cyclotomic-type multiplier survives, matches known facts about congruence quotients. It shows his working method but contains no result absent from the literature.
